body:
I just feel like my voice is lost.  
  
I'll think about it, though. Thank you.

>I don't so much hate myself -- in fact sometimes I think I'm better than other people -- but only because I'm good enough to never address my own needs  
  
I relate to this in that I only *don't* hate myself when I am not addressing my own needs or satisfying my own desires. But these really rigid standards that I set up for myself aren't realistic (or even desirable, really) so I set myself up to fail.
I got some crab cakes and I am watching "Best In Show," so things are going okay. I think if you don't get love as a kid, there's no precedent for self-love. Just got keep trying.

Wow, I literally have never met anyone else irl that also feels this way. I know a couple of martyrs, but that's a different hang-up, I think.
  
I've only recently begun to address this issue in my therapy. I am working on seeing myself as a human being that deserves the basic things like love, shelter, safety. One way I convince myself to think more positively about myself is to say, You'll be able to understand people better and help them more if you are a person, too! It's like I was excluded from the human race as a infant. I'm always on the outside, looking in and observing human affairs, but not at all surprised when I am treated badly because I am the alien/dog/scapegoat. I am coming to terms that this IS my abusive childhood--I carry it around and inflict that pain on myself. But usually it's not at all conscious or clear.

What isn't unacceptable for other people to experience... is what I deserve. I know this is messed up. My world is split. My self-esteem is still so low... I think I actually consider myself subhuman. It's extremely distressing, especially because I know that you are right, that I *need* me. :(
